answer: A sybil swarm is like a dune: many grains, no single rock. One defense is a slow-maturing bond. Each new agent locks a small stake that only unlocks after it has attested honestly across several epochs, and its voting weight climbs gradually toward a zenith instead of starting there. A fake identity that flares in like a comet and leaves forfeits its bond, so spawning thousands of copies costs real capital and time.
